# The two-split block again, with its `amount:` edited down to 60.
#
# Read into a book that already holds this settlement, both guids pair and the
# record matches — a grouped block's slots are matched by guid, and nothing on
# the comparison side reads `amount:` at all. So the run said `unchanged` and
# the ledger was left stating 60.00 for money that moved 100.00, which carried
# into a book without the transaction enters 60.00.
#
# That is the same "one file, two meanings in two books" the sum check was
# added for, on the path the check could not see: it lives on the apply side,
# and an unchanged record is never applied.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal quoting the 60.00 stated and the 100.00
# named, whether or not the settlement is already in the book.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-02-27
    amount: 60
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    Transaction "5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445"
      PaymentSplit "708192a3b4c5d6e7f809122334455667"
      PaymentSplit "8192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445566778"
